grammar.label: the former, the latter and the aforementioned
grammar.form: the former … the latter; the aforementioned + noun
grammar.meaning: points back to two things already named, in order

explanation.en: 'The former' is the first of two just mentioned, 'the latter' the second. They work only with exactly two, and only when the reader can still hold both in mind. 'The aforementioned' points back to something named earlier and is heavily formal.
explanation.uz: 'the former' — ikkitaning birinchisi, 'the latter' — ikkinchisi. Faqat aynan ikkita narsa bo'lganda ishlaydi. 'the aforementioned' — yuqorida aytilgan narsaga ishora, juda rasmiy.

grammar.positive_example: We considered cost and time; the former was decisive.
grammar.negative_example: We considered cost, time and staffing; the former was decisive.

l1_notes.uz: Uchta yoki undan ko'p narsa bo'lsa, bu juftlik ishlatilmaydi — nomini takrorlash kerak.

grammar.label: this, that and such as cohesive reference
grammar.form: this / that / such + noun, referring back to a whole idea
grammar.meaning: packages what was just said so the next sentence can use it

explanation.en: A bare 'This shows…' leaves the reader guessing what 'this' is. Adding a noun labels it: 'This finding shows…', 'Such delays are common.' The label is the writer's summary, and choosing it is an act of argument.
explanation.uz: Yolg'iz 'This shows…' o'quvchini chalg'itadi. Ot qo'shilsa, nimaga ishora qilinayotgani aniq bo'ladi: 'This finding shows…'. Tanlangan ot — muallifning xulosasi.

grammar.positive_example: This pattern held for three years.
grammar.negative_example: This held for three years, which shows the pattern.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida ishora olmoshi otsiz ham tabiiy; ingliz ilmiy uslubida esa ot qo'shish kutiladi.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I have two versions, a long one and a short one.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: The former for the ministry, the latter for the village?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The other way round. The village wants the detail.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then say which is which, because the reader cannot see your desk.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is my trouble with 'the former'. It makes the reader count back up the page.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Use it when the two things are one line apart, never three paragraphs.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: 'Such' is useful. It picks up a whole idea in one word. 'The road closed for six weeks. Such a delay costs a harvest.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: A gift is free. That is a tautology. Cut one word.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And 'at the end of the day'?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: A platitude. Say what you mean, or say nothing and save the line.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The page is a third shorter.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And twice as clear. Concision is not leaving things out. It is leaving out what was never doing any work.
